readingOfTheCodePaths.source: studio-runner/src/run/launcher.ts L405-482 and run/childRuntime.ts finish() L150-185, read only
facts: The launcher picks INTERNAL_ERROR when there is no child result errorCode, no abort, and the wait settled (exit or IPC violation). It also passes through a child-sent errorCode of INTERNAL_ERROR, because a child-sent reason wins.
The child's finish() always sends a 'result' message before channel.exit(0) when a launch was received.
readingOfTheCodePaths.inference: The child exited through finish(), because the exit wrapper sealed the sample. So one of two things happened. (a) The child reported errorCode INTERNAL_ERROR for an unmapped exception in its own pre-Ready path. That path is wrapped by the test preload: the playwrightBrowserFactory.launch wrapper, the initial-context check, the createObservationSession wrapper, the p4NativeCloseObserverSdk observers, and the producer-3 process.on/send/exit wrappers. (b) The parent rejected that result as a protocol violation (violation=true, result unset). The retained artifacts cannot tell (a) from (b): the runner logs neither the child errorCode nor the violation branch. Either way, instrumentation interference with the child pre-Ready path or IPC is now a live suspect, not just host load.

diagnosticsR10b.approvedBy: root via coordinator, diagnostics only: Order(1) + kind 1 with a tap, scratch-only, up to 8 attempts, then under load; measure the p6ChildCutSpawner per-send mode-file read.
method: An out-of-tree Gradle init script excludes the repo GuidedPublicationReplayIT.java from compileTestJava by absolute path and compiles a scratch copy instead. The scratch copy is generated by a patch script that fails unless every anchor matches exactly once. Selector: --tests Order(1) actualLearningPublishesWithoutEffectsThenTwoOrdinaryRunsRecaptureFreshValues + actualPublishedNativePasswordStepDeadlinePreservesUnknownEffect, test --rerun.

Child tap: the ordinary launcher forks a scratch entry (named recorded-child.mjs.r10-entry.mjs so the test still finds its child by command line). The entry installs a Node module-customization load hook that rewrites dist/run/childRuntime.js IN MEMORY ONLY (hookApplied=3 in every run). Three calls are added: the dispatch catch (original exception name/constructor/code/frames), finish(errorCode) and stop(code). It also wraps process.send to record ready/result kind+errorCode. dist/run/browser.js (the hashed launcher file) is untouched.

Parent tap (scratch copy of ordinary.mjs): per spawned child, every IPC message kind received (result errorCode/ok plus a Result3 schema check with the runner validator), every send, every handle.kill() call with call-site frames, and exit code/signal. The frames separate the launcher protocol-violation catch from performStop grace kill. Also synchronous timings: the p6ChildCutSpawner revMode() read and the producer-2 revMode() read on control GETs, the whole synchronous control-GET send, every producer-2 revPublish, control-read send-to-settle, and a monitorEventLoopDelay histogram (resolution 10 ms) from spawn to child exit. Data is written once per child, asynchronously, at child exit.

cutSpawnerModeReadCost.what: p6ChildCutSpawner revHttp.send wrapper: synchronous revMode() (existsSync + readFileSync + JSON.parse) on every send; measured only on control GETs
cutSpawnerModeReadCost.verified: Across 17 valid kind-1 runs (44-48 control GETs each): per-read p50 0.064-0.124 ms, per-run max 0.2-5.8 ms. The producer-2 revMode() read on the same GETs: per-run max 0.07-15.4 ms (15.4 ms once under heavy load). The whole synchronous control-GET send (all wrappers + real client send) per-run max 1.1-60.4 ms.
cutSpawnerModeReadCost.assessment: Small compared with the producer-2 synchronous revPublish (max 458.7 ms) and with control-read latency under load (max 1198 ms). It is not zero under load, though: one read of 5.8 ms, and a 15.4 ms producer-2 read once.

caveats: monitorEventLoopDelay at resolution 10 ms reports values that include the ~10 ms sampling interval (quiet-run mean ~10.6 ms); subtract ~10 ms for excess delay. Its window is spawn to child exit, so it includes post-outcome close.
controlRead is measured from send to settle as observed on the parent loop, so it includes parent loop delay.
The tap adds a then() on each control-GET promise (timing push only) and per-call performance.now() pairs. Their cost is in the microseconds but non-zero.
Isolation (Order(1)+kind 1) does not carry the full-class worker preload state that run 3 had (kind 1 ran after ~29 earlier cases in the same long-lived workers).
